body.p: There was a man, his name is Charchikan. He stole the children of the stupid bird Kingit. She brought him to her home. She brought him [to her] home. [She has] three children. He looked for the children. The children played with Charchikan [with his hairs?]. Two [or] three years passed. When this was (?), Kingit landed; sitting there, Kingit was crying. "Why do you cry?", the man asked. Kingit said: "Why do you ask me, [instead] of calming, you son of a dog." He asked for a long time; he got tired of asking the bird. "Tomorrow at noon a thunder will probably destroy the house", Kingit said, "it will probably kill the children." "I would hide the children, for that it doesn't kill them", the man said and went off. It became morning, the man led her children to a distant country, far away. He reached [brought] her children's heads (?). They can't pick Charchikan[]'s] [hairs] (?). When he was arriving, the thunder started. Going, the thunder broke the whole mountain, the children died soon, but they revived again. After the thunder has stopped, they are living, Kingit came crying, she is searching her children. She found her children, she was happy. She took her children, she took the game that they were playing, she repaired the house. Kingit asked the human: "For the children's rescue, in which land do you want go now?" Charchikan said: "Bring me up, into a hole in the sky." "A big torture, our way", Kingit said. Kingit brought two animals with naked antlers and said: "When I'll beg you, put [them] into my mouth." Now she flew off, she took Charchikan along. Going and gliding she flows up. They went [=flew] for four say, the hole in the sky could be seen. Kingit said: "Don't tell, if you meet someone, [that] Kingit has brought you." She let the man down, the man went off. A big land, good, with grass, there is no human trace, there is nothing. He is living, he is walking. Then he saw, a house is standing there, he went to the house and reached it. A woman lives there, she is sleeping; a good woman, beautiful, she is sewing. He asked, the woman didn't hear. "Why does the fire crackle?", the woman said, she doesn't see the man. Three, four days the man was living, he ate food. "Why the food is running out?", the woman said. So he was living, he wanted to sleep [with her]. In the night he crawled onto her and began to sleep with the woman. He was going (?), the man slept with the woman (?). There the woman felt and saw the man. "What did bring you here? Did Kingit bring [you]?" "I myself came." "Now you made me [commit] a sin. You can't live here now, there is no land. Bring some earth [clay] from the ground", the woman said. The man said: "How shall I bring [it]?" The woman gave [him] a winged horse, the man went off. The woman said: "Whom who meet, if they say [something], don't listen, hurry, come back, my horse will bring you." She tied him to the horse. The horse went down through the hole. They go [=fly] to the earth. They reached the earth. He fell down onto a path. An old woman has upset her sledge, she can't turn it over. Charchikan fell down beneath the sledge. Seeing him the old woman said: "Help, help, turn the sledge over." The man got untied from the horse, he took his harness, he turned the sledge over, he helped the old woman." The old woman took Charchikan by his hand. "I said: Three years are lost. The death took him. In three years he wore out the shoes and the sledge." Charchikan looked, the horse flew back. When the horse had arrived, he heard the words: "You made me [commit] a sin, I have said to you: "don't listen", you didn't listen to me."
